title: Residency acceptance test catalog and operator primer
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical acceptance-test catalog and operator primer for verifying data residency behavior during staging and production rollouts. It is intended for engineers performing preflight checks (SRE/infra), solutions engineers validating customer pins, and oncall operators responding to residency alerts.

Scope:
- Focus on region pin enforcement, fallback routes, evidence capture, and observable side-effects (latency, errors, audit logs).
- Tests assume a private deployment or dedicated environment with region-pin metadata support and routing controls.
- Not a full security audit; complements existing legal checklist.

How to use this document:
- Run the canonical tests below during every major residency change (region-pin policy update, routing service rollout, HA configuration change).
- For each test, capture the listed telemetry and attach to incident or PR.
- Mark tests PASS/FAIL and file a follow-up ticket with trace ids and artifacts.

Acceptance test catalog (canonical cases) - quick index:
1) Tenant pin enforcement (happy path)
2) Cross-region request rejection / explicit error
3) Graceful fallback to approved region variant
4) Stale KV cache causing mis-routing
5) Edge-case: mixed-region multi-request transaction
6) Region pin migration (rolling update)
7) Operator eviction (forced failover)
8) Residency evidence packaging for audit
9) Telemetry spike and sampling sanity
10) Compliance exception handling

1) Tenant pin enforcement (happy path)
- Objective: Confirm requests for tenant T with region=eu-west-1 are routed to eu-west-1 hosts only and all storage writes are anchored there.
- Preconditions: Tenant has active region pin; eu-west pool healthy; test user account with synthetic payloads.
- Steps: Issue 50 short requests and 20 generation requests (varied seq length). Verify route headers show eu-west-1; confirm storage write stream endpoints.
- Expected: 100% routing to eu-west-1; no fallbacks. Audit log entries contain tenant pin id, route decision, and operator id=null.
- Monitoring signals: per-tenant route_count, route_mismatch_count=0, storage_write_region histogram.
- Evidence to collect: request IDs, route headers, audit log excerpt, server allocation trace.

2) Cross-region request rejection / explicit error
- Objective: Ensure requests originating from forbidden region return clear error (HTTP 403 / RESIDENCY_VIOLATION) and do not leak processing.
- Steps: Simulate request with geo header outside pinned territory; observe client-facing error and internal traces.
- Expected: 403 with residency error code, no downstream model invocation logs, token usage metric 0.

3) Graceful fallback to approved region variant
- Objective: Validate automatic fallback when primary pool is degraded but a compliant variant exists (e.g., quantized offline model in same region).
- Preconditions: Primary model in eu-west unhealthy; fallback variant deployed.
- Expected: Traffic flip to fallback with alert and annotated audit event. SLA degradation metric increased but data locality preserved.

4) Stale KV cache causing mis-routing
- Rationale: Frequent cause of silent mis-routing after pin changes.
- Steps: Deploy pin change, but deliberately delay cache invalidation on a subset of nodes; run requests; confirm mismatch rate and correct invalidation steps.
- Rollback trigger: mismatch_rate > 1% sustained for 10m.

5) Mixed-region multi-request transaction
- Objective: Test session-scoped workflows spanning multiple requests where pins differ mid-session (e.g., user moves region or tenant pin updated).
- Expected: Either session-level pin enforcement (reject or rebind) or clear migration log.

6) Region pin migration (rolling update)
- Steps: Execute scripted migration from region A to B for a customer under canary; validate plan below: 1) dry-run telemetry only, 2) canary 5% traffic, 3) ramp to 25%, 4) full cutover.
- Test artifacts: migration diffs, pre/post route histogram, customer-visible latency delta.

7) Operator eviction (forced failover)
- Objective: Simulate operator-triggered eviction (manual node drain) and verify pinned tenants remain anchored to allowed region (i.e., failover to same-region substitute, not to other region).

8) Residency evidence packaging for audit
- Template: tenant_id, request_ids sample (n=50), route_headers, audit_log_slice, deployment manifest hash, signed operator action id.
- Note: make sure evidence is tamper-evident (hash bundle) and stored in compliance blobstore.

9) Telemetry spike and sampling sanity
- Validate that sampling remains representative during high QPS and that residency sampling retains 100% for policy-decision events (do not sample away).

10) Compliance exception handling
- Validate the exception flow (approved by compliance) that allows temporary cross-region processing. Ensure expiration, approval id, and operator actions are logged and auto-reverted.

Enforcement policy quick matrix (operator reference):
- If routing decision would send data outside pinned region: BLOCK and return RESIDENCY_VIOLATION unless explicit exception exists.
- If primary resource unavailable and same-region variant exists: FAILOVER to variant and create PostMortemCandidate=true.
- If no same-region fallback: Return RESIDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with guidance to customer.

Operator oncall checklist (short):
- On residency alert (route_mismatch_count > 0): 1) pull trace ids 2) run acceptance test #1 for affected tenant 3) check KV invalidation job status 4) inspect operator action log 5) if mismatch persists, execute emergency rollback to previous routing config
- Evidence grab: download audit bundle, include deployment manifest and operator IDs.

Telemetry & dashboards recommended signals:
- per-tenant route_count, route_mismatch_count, fallback_count, residency_error_rate, storage_write_region histogram, audit_event_rate, sampling_coverage_percent.
- Dashboard panels: Recent mismatches (with traces), migration progress, canary failure percent, evidence bundles ready.

Common failure modes and diagnostics tips:
- Symptoms: sudden spike in route_mismatch_count after release -> likely cache invalidation or config push order.
- Symptom: partial mismatches only on long requests -> check gateway-level streaming proxies and header propagation.
- Symptom: audit logs present but missing operator id -> misconfigured auth or ephemeral creds for automation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical signed evidence format (currently working w/ compliance). TODO: finalise JSON+signature schema.
- Add synthetic workloads for large-seq generation to migration test (#6).
- Automation: create a test runner that can execute items 1-4 automatically with artifacts upload.

Appendix: quick commands & links
- Local test runner: github.com/redwood-inference/pinning-e2e (branch: acceptance)
- Compliance reference doc: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Migration playbook template: CONFLUENCE-574

Notes: This is a working doc — expect edits after the next compliance sync. If you run tests, attach the raw evidence bundle to the linked JIRA ticket (JIRA-PIN-987) and ping the privacy-compliance channel.
